On 23.10.2025, the Nodal Officer of this Court recorded the video clippings regarding the state of paver blocks by the side of the Taladanda Canal and garbage stacked in and around Urban Hat area.
The video also indicated rapid growth of bushes along the Taladanda Canal towards Nuabazar which was largely due to lack of steps taken to clear bushes, lack of monitoring and of proper maintenance.
This Court had directed the CMC authorities to clear the same immediately and to ensure that the entire stretch is lighted properly and sought response of the concerned officials on these issues.

In the report dated 30.10.2025 of the Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation) CMC, it is stated that so far as bush cutting by the side of Taladanda Canal is concerned, the same is being undertaken by CMC along the Taladanda Canal and now, the bush cutting work is under progress.
Similarly, the garbage in and around Urban Hat is being cleaned on regular interval.
Mr. Avijit Patnaik, Secretary, High Court of Orissa has filed a memo along with photographs depicting accumulation of garbage in ward nos.4, 18, 19, 27, 28, 29, 39, 47, 52, which are taken on record.
Copies of the photographs has handed over to the learned counsel for the CMC, who seeks some time to obtain instruction on the same.

The photographs of accumulation of garbage in different wards show that "all is not well"
with the activities of the three agencies, who are charging more than three crores every month and in spite of payment of penalty for their laches, are not mending their activities.
When the three agencies have received more than 28 crores as per agreement in last nine months, the penalty amount of around Rs.70 lakhs would not have created much impact on them.

During the deliberation, it was brought to the notice of this Court that Mr. Behera,
Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation), CMC was earlier working as Executive Officer of Hinjilicut Municipality and he has joined on 27.09.2025.

During the discussions, Mr.
Behera, Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation), CMC apprises this Court that there are certain practices relating to sanitation activities, which were adopted when he was the Executive Officer of Hinjilicut Municipality, which showed remarkable results in addressing the problems relating to sanitation to a great extent and during his short tenure as the Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation), CMC, he has noticed certain shortcomings in the sanitation programmes of the CMC.

He has assured this Court that he is in the process of discussing with the concerned agencies so that the issues relating to sanitation can be addressed in an effective manner justifying the huge amount spent on sanitation.

sentences.text: During the proceeding, learned President and Secretary of the Orissa High Court Bar Association drew the attention of the Court that in most of the areas of different wards, no dustbins have been provided by the CMC for which there is no scope to put the garbage in the designated place and which is also resulting in dumping of the same on the public roads.
Mr. Behera, Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation), CMC states that a conscious decision was taken to remove the dustbins because they became the dumping points.

There is no dispute that dustbins are used in urban areas for garbage collection to prevent littering, maintain public health and aesthetics, and support waste management through proper disposal and recycling.

They provide a central place for citizens to discard waste, which helps in controlling the spread of diseases, reduces the negative impact of litter on the environment, and is often more cost- effective and durable than other options.

Of course, disadvantage of dustbins include public health risks from overflowing bins and attracting pests and other environmental issues on account of air and water pollution from decomposition and improper disposal.

This Court calls upon the Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation), CMC to explore the possibility of putting the dustbins as a test case in some places in different wards and to evaluate the sanitation position.
In the event, the installation of such dustbins facilitate better management of garbage, the same may be explored on a regular basis.
This aspect shall be considered on the next sitting.

Concern was expressed by the President and Secretary of the Orissa High Court Bar Association regarding the use of polythene which is posing hazards including clogged drains and water logging, which can spread waterborne diseases like malaria and dengue.
Burning polythene releases toxic gases that cause air pollution, respiratory issues and even cancer.

Non-biodegradable polythene also pollutes land and water,
harms animals, and its microplastics can enter the food chain and human bodies,
potentially causing long- term health problems like hormonal disruption and cancer.
It was submitted that this issue needs to be addressed on emergency basis during upcoming Baliyatra.

Alternatives to plastic bags include reusable bags made of cotton, jute, or canvas,
which are durable and washable.
For food storage, options like reusable silicone or beewax-lined bags, along with glass containers are preferable.
Other alternatives include recycled paper bags and various types of bio-degradable and compostable bags, such as those made from plant-based materials like starch or bamboo.

Mr. Shibo Toppo, ADM, Cuttack, who is present through virtual mode, has assured this Court that necessary steps for sensitization and administrative steps to stop the use of polythene in Baliyatra shall be taken and viable alternatives which are Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others .... Mr. Avijit Patnaik, Secretary, High Court of Orissa has filed a memo along with a news item published in the vernacular Odia daily dated 28.10.2025, under the heading of "URBAN HATARE GURUTARA ABYABASTHA, MASAKU DASA LAKHYA; TANKA AADAYA KARI BASI JAUCHI CMC" (Serious Disorder in Urban Market, Monthly collection of Rs.10 lakh; CMC collecting money and sitting idle),
wherein it is mentioned that the Urban Hat is facing extreme disorder in terms of cleanliness and management.
The CMC is collecting dues from small and large traders inside the Urban Hat.
Even bicycles and motorcycles parked on the footpath outside the market are being charged parking fees.
However, the CMC authorities have forgotten to provide basic amenities in the Urban Hat.
Garbage is not being removed from the market.
Unauthorized trucks are parked on the road inside the market for loading and unloading goods.
Persons are sitting and selling goods inside the market in vehicles.
Parking arrangements with payable fees have been made on the footpath paved with paver blocks outside the market.
A fee of Rs.10/- is being collected for parking two-wheelers.
There is no drinking water facility.
Yet, the CMC is collecting Rs.15,000/- to 20,000/- daily from traders in the market.
About Rs.20,000/- is also collected daily for vehicle parking.
In this way, the urban market collects more than Rs.10 lakh monthly.
However, the basic facilities of the Urban Hat remain neglected.
The memo along with the news item is taken on record.

Relating to the lack of basic amenities in Urban Hat area, Mr. Debasis Nayak, learned counsel for the CMC assures this Court that the same shall be looked into along with the District Administration to take steps to provide a toilet complex and also make provision of safe drinking water.

It is also brought to the notice of this Court by the Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation), CMC that taking into account the concern expressed regarding the unhygienic condition of Urban Hat, now cleaning is taking place once every two hours and such cleaning is being monitored and photographs are taken and circulated in a Whatsapp group created for such purpose.

Mr. Avijit Patnaik, Secretary, High Court of 30.10.2025 Orissa has filed a memo along with a news item published in the vernacular Odia daily dated 29.10.2025, under the heading of "CUTTACK BADA DAKTARAKHANA, DAIBA BHARASARE ROGI SAMPARKIYA", wherein it is stated that SCBMCH, Cuttack is facing many fundamental problems.
The relatives of the patients coming here are facing many difficulties.
Due to the lack of necessary night shelter, they are spending the night in unsafe conditions outside the hospital premises.

Taking advantage of this,
thieves are cunningly roaming around the patients' relatives and robbing mobile phones, jewellery,
money, and cash.
As a result, the patients and their relatives have to face harassment.
Even during the rainy and cold days, it has been observed that the patients' relatives spend the night here, relying on charity.
People have immense faith in SCBMCH, Cuttack.
Every day, huge numbers of patients come here from within and outside the State with hope for good treatment.
SCBMCH, Cuttack has become a refuge for poor, helpless, and critically ill patients.

Over time, the stature of SCBMCH,
Cuttack has increased.
It has achieved many successes in treating patients with modern medical methods.
Now, SCBMCH, Cuttack is being expanded and developed as an M.S. Plus, which can be connected as a major medical institution in eastern India.
In this situation, if fundamental problems in SCBMCH, Cuttack could not be resolved, its impact would be on the patients and their relatives.
Due to the lack of necessary testing machines and their non- functioning, patients have to wait for hours at the testing centres.

Moreover, there is no waiting area or night shelter for patients'
relatives.
Therefore, relatives spend the night outside the wards or on the roadside near the hospital.
While the Women and Maternity Department and the Orthopaedic Department have two night shelters nearby, other wards do not have any night shelter facilities.

Many departments like the Emergency Department and Neurology Department also lack shelter facilities and therefore, the relatives of the patients spend the night in front of the wards, on the steps or in the corridors.
Since these places are not under CCTV surveillance, the risk of theft is increasing, and thieves are not caught.
There is also a concern about undesirable incidents of misconduct.

While SCBMCH, Cuttack is being expanded, special emphasis should be given to providing night shelters, drinking water, and toilet facilities as necessary, so that patients and their relatives can benefit.
Especially, many patients' relatives have appealed that the State Government should pay special attention to this aspect.
The memo along with the news item is taken on record.
A copy of the news item has been handed over to the learned counsel for the State.

sentences.text: " 1 . No. of PwD Students

It is submitted that actually there are 77 students of PwD category in the Sailabala Women's College, Cuttack for this academic year out of which number of Under Graduate students is 31, post Graduate students is 10 and Higher Secondary School Student is 36.

2. Types of Disability It is revealed that out of 77 students, 3 are orthopedically handicapped/locomotor disability, one from neurological disorder, one is suffering from dwarfism and the rest 72 are visually challenged.
Being a Women's College
, all the students are girls.
In December, 2015, the college had built a hostel dedicated exclusively for the students with disability.
It is a G +1 building having provision of lift.

When the team constituted as per the order of this Court, visited the college on 17.10.25, 16 students with disability were already accommodated in M.S. PH Hostel and 39 were accommodated in other general hostels.
3. Dedicated Hostel facility

Taking a serious note of the fact that 39 students are accommodated in General Hostels and in consideration to the requirement of the students with disability, it is immediately decided to shift these students with disability numbering 39 (28 M.S Old Hostel + 04 M.S. PG Hostel + 07 S.B New Hostel) to the physically challenged hostel exclusively meant for them which is having the capacity for 60 students.
The rest 22 students with disability are not boarders.

Although it is a hostel for students with disability, it is found that to make it completely habitable for them with facilities necessary for such students, the inadequacy, if any, will be modified and proper facilities will be installed to make it habitable and conducive for the students with disability.
This process has already been started by WATCO Division, Cuttack from 28.10.25 and will be completed within a day or two.

A joint meeting was convened on 25.10.2025, in the Office chamber of the Director Higher Education, where the decision was taken to immediately shift the 39 nos. of students with disability to M.S. PH Hostel, exclusively meant for them.

Accordingly,
an urgent meeting of the Residential Committee was convened under the chairmanship of the Principal, vide notice no.1915 dtd.25.10.2025, at 4.00 p.m. on 25.10.2025, in presence of all members of the Residential Committee of the college.
It was unanimously resolved to shift 39 nos. of students of different hostels to M.S. PH Hostel (rest 16 nos. of students are staying in the M.S. PH Hostel).
On 26th October 2025, in presence of Superintendents of different hostels, initiative was made to shift all those 39 nos. of students to M.S. PH Hostel.

At the time of shifting, disabled students of M.S. Old Hostel submitted an application, which was duly forwarded by the Superintendent of the said hostel, stating that they were not willing to shift from their parent hostel with a contention that, the facilities they are getting in that hostel will not be available in the hostel they are likely to be shifted.

They have also emphasized on the NEP 2020 policy, which aims to bring parity for students with Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others .... Opp. ... on 30 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187702225/

sentences.text: The policy draws heavily on the rights of persons with disabilities (PwD Act, 2016) and focuses on moving away from a segregated system towards mainstream inclusive education.

They have also mentioned that intellectual development of students with disabilities (PwDs) from the psychological standpoint, which involves creating an inclusive and supportive environment through Individualized Education Plans (IEPS), differentiated instruction, as well as to promote a positive attitude in the staff and peers.

Further, integrating them with general students in hostels offers them significant social, academic and personal development benefits, which includes increased sense of belongingness, improved social and communication skills, enhanced independence, wider social network, greater empathy and acceptance, reduced prejudice and stereotyping, so as to develop compassion, team work, new perspectives and problem-solving skills in them.
Therefore, only 06 disabled students of S.B. New Hostel and 01 student from M.S. PG Hostel were shifted to M.S. PH Hostel exclusively meant for them.
Appreciating the request of 39 such students who are in the General Hostels they are given the liberty to stay in their choice of Hostels.
4. Special Path-ways
Since it is a hostel meant for the students with disability, it has all the requisite facilities required for the purpose.

It is observed that when the hostel was constructed in the year 2015, it lacked tactile pathways inside the hostel as well as the approach road leading from the academic block of the college as well as in the campus.

The Assistant Executive Engineer, and Assistant Engineer PWD (R & B), RP line, Buxibazar, Cuttack have visited the campus and have assured to start the work of laying the tactile path, construction of ramps with railings, construction of disabled- friendly toilets, etc., very soon after taking measurements and submission of estimate.
The work will be taken up on war footing basis and completed within a month time.

It was discussed that for the benefit of such students, the classrooms used by them will be relocated on the ground floor of the academic floor so that the students with disability will not have much difficulties in accessing the classrooms and the student who has to go to the other building located outside the boundary of the main building, will also have their classroom in the main building.
5. Inaccessible Class Rooms & Library
However, this is a century old educational institution accommodated in the residential complex of late Sri Madhusudan Das and Late Miss Shailabala Das in the centre of the City.
Due to the lack of space, horizontal expansion of the College is not possible.
Apart from this, this is a composite college offering courses from +2 to P.G, utilizing the limited number of rooms with same infrastructure, for all the courses.

the students must opt for other electives and one MIL of their choice and therefore, bringing all their classes to the ground floor is not practically feasible, while restricting their choice for electives will be unfair to them.

whereas departments of Botany, Chemistry, Odia and Pol. Science are on 1st floors.
However, the departments of Economics and Education are on the 2nd floor, while the department of English is on the 3rd floor of Arts Academic building.
Persistent efforts have been made to install the lift facility in the said Arts Academic building by the institution, which is likely to get materialized very soon.
But as student of chemistry must attend practical classes in the laboratory, it is practically impossible to bring it down to the ground floor.

Due to the lack of necessary night shelter, they are spending the night in unsafe conditions outside the hospital premises.
Taking advantage of this,
thieves are cunningly roaming around the patients' relatives and robbing mobile phones, jewellery,
money, and cash.
As a result, the patients and their relatives have to face harassment.
Even during the rainy and cold days, it has been observed that the patients' relatives spend the night here, relying on charity.
People have immense faith in SCBMCH, Cuttack.
Every day, huge numbers of patients come here from within and outside the State with hope for good treatment.
SCBMCH, Cuttack has become a refuge for poor, helpless, and critically ill patients.
Over time, the stature of SCBMCH,
Cuttack has increased.
It has achieved many successes in treating patients with modern medical methods.
Now, SCBMCH, Cuttack is being expanded and developed as an M.S. Plus, which can be connected as a major medical institution in eastern India.
In this situation, if fundamental problems in SCBMCH, Cuttack could not be resolved, its impact would be on the patients and their relatives.
Due to the lack of necessary testing machines and their non- functioning, patients have to wait for hours at the testing centres.
Moreover, there is no waiting area or night shelter for patients'
relatives.
Therefore, relatives spend the night outside the wards or on the roadside near the hospital.
While the Women and Maternity Department and the Orthopaedic Department have two night shelters nearby, other wards do not have any night shelter facilities.
Many departments like the Emergency Department and Neurology Department also lack shelter facilities and therefore, the relatives of the patients spend the night in front of the wards, on the steps or in the corridors.
Since these places are not under CCTV surveillance, the risk of theft is increasing, and thieves are not caught.
There is also a concern about undesirable incidents of misconduct.
While SCBMCH, Cuttack is being expanded, special emphasis should be given to providing night shelters, drinking water, and toilet facilities as necessary, so that patients and their relatives can benefit.
